case_name: Lal Singh v State Of Gujarat & Anr.
facts: After trial in TADA Case Nos. 2/93, 7/93 and 2/94, by judgment and order dated 08 January, 1997, the Designated Judge, Ahmadabad (Rural) at Mirzapur, Ahmadabad, acquitted 16 accused and convicted 5 accused, appellants herein, namely, A1 Lal Singh, A2 Mohd. Sharief, A3 Tahir Jamal, A4 Mohd. Saquib Nachan and A20 Shoaib Mukhtiar.

The appellants were convicted for the offences punishable (1) u/s. 3 (3) of Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act, 1987 (hereinafter referred to as TADA Act) and sentenced to suffer life imprisonment and to pay a fine of Rs. 10,000/- each and in default to suffer R.I. for 6 months; (2) under Section 120B (1) of IPC and sentenced to suffer R.I for 10 years and to pay a fine of Rs. 5000/- each, in default to suffer R.I. for 3 months.
All sentences were directed to run concurrently.
According to prosecution, in the year 1984 the terrorism had gone beyond limits and therefore, blue star operation was performed.
It is further stated that A1 and A4 visited Madras to survey the stock exchange building to find out the possibility of bomb blast there.
The statements lend support to prove the conspiracy.
Accused no. 1 Lal Singh was arrested in the morning of 16 July 1992 at Dadar Railway Station while he was alighting from a train.
On receipt of the said information, Mr. Anopkumar Singh rushed to the Commissioner of Police, Baroda.
The C.P. Baroda also talked about the information with Mr. Surolia, DCP Ahmadabad (PW103).
Finally, after completing the investigation accused were charge-sheeted and tried by the Designated Judge at Ahmadabad.
All the accused persons abjured their guilt, pleaded innocence and stated that they have been falsely implicated in this case.
issues: What is the nature of the conspiracy?
Was the evidence sufficient to prove the charges?
Did the appellants receive a fair trial?
petitioner_arguments: The appellants were convicted for the offences punishable (1) u/s. 3 (3) of Terrorist and Disruptive Activities (Prevention) Act, 1987 (hereinafter referred to as TADA Act) and sentenced to suffer life imprisonment and to pay a fine of Rs. 10,000/- each and in default to suffer R.I. for 6 months; (2) under Section 120B (1) of IPC and sentenced to suffer R.I for 10 years and to pay a fine of Rs. 5000/- each, in default to suffer R.I. for 3 months.
All sentences were directed to run concurrently.
respondent_arguments: The prosecution examined 136 witnesses during the trial and relied upon various documents including confessional statements recorded during investigation.
court_reasoning: The evidence against A3, A4 and A20 shows that they were helping and abetting A1 and A2 in common design.
The statements lend support to prove the conspiracy.
It is further stated that A1 to A4 and A20, in their respective confessional statements, corroborate with each other on various points and items of conspiracy.
holding: The Designated Judge, Ahmadabad (Rural) at Mirzapur, Ahmadabad, acquitted 16 accused and convicted 5 accused, appellants herein, namely, A1 Lal Singh, A2 Mohd. Sharief, A3 Tahir Jamal, A4 Mohd. Saquib Nachan and A20 Shoaib Mukhtiar.
